sentences.text: Revenue (net interest income plus noninterest income) rose from $96.6 billion in FY2016 to $182 billion in FY2025, an 8.4% net interest income CAGR and 6.2% noninterest income CAGR [D5][D206][F111][F112].
The path was a step change, not a smooth compound: revenue was $120 billion in FY2020, $122 billion in FY2021, then $158 billion in FY2023 and $178 billion in FY2024 [D86][D110][D159][D183].
The FY2022-FY2023 jump came from net interest income, which grew 27.5% then 33.8%, while interest income rose from $92.8 billion to $170.6 billion [D149][D174][X124][X125].
FY2025 growth slowed to 2.8%, with net interest income up 3.1% on higher Markets net interest income and Card revolving balances, largely offset by deposit margin compression [D226][D221][P28].
North America remains the core at 76.6% of revenue in FY2025, but contributed only 0.2pp of growth that year versus 20.6pp in FY2023 [D249][D251][D245].
International is now the faster grower: EMEA added 1.2pp and Asia-Pacific 1.2pp in FY2025, with Asia-Pacific revenue up 17.3% [D276][D301][D300].

The FY2025 noninterest income rise of 2.4% reflected higher Markets revenue, asset management fees and a $588 million First Republic-related gain, offset by the absence of the prior year's $7.9 billion Visa gain [D222][P27].
Profit did not keep pace: net income fell 2.6% in FY2025 while revenue rose 2.8%, and the provision for credit losses rose to $14.2 billion from $10.7 billion [D214][D226][X147][X146].
Per-share growth outran net income over the window, with diluted EPS compounding at 13.9% against net income at 9.7%, helped by a 3.4% share-count reduction in FY2025 [F115][F113][D224].
The efficiency ratio was 52.4% in FY2025, better than the 57.2% window median but above the 51.7% FY2024 low [D207][D333][D331].

Against seven bank peers the efficiency ratio sits at the 0th percentile versus a 61.7% median, while return on average equity of 16.1% is at the 100th percentile against an 11.8% median [D336][D337][D213][D338][D339].

Noninterest expense rose 4.2% in FY2025, driven by higher compensation, brokerage and distribution fees, and technology and marketing investment, partly offset by FDIC special assessment releases [D225][P26].
Credit costs are the offset: the provision was 7.8% of revenue in FY2025 against a 6.0% peer median, at the 75th percentile [D208][D341][D340].
Net margin held at 31.2% of revenue in FY2025, with a 21.4% effective tax rate close to the 22.1% of FY2024 [D210][D203][D180].
For a bank, operating cash flow is not a meaningful earnings-quality measure; it was negative $148 billion in FY2025 against $57.0 billion of net income [F60][F30].
The FY2025 outflow resulted from higher trading assets, higher securities borrowed, and net originations and purchases of loans held-for-sale [P21].
Capital return is the better gauge: buybacks plus dividends of $48.2 billion in FY2025 were 85% of net income, up from $33.6 billion in FY2024 [D205][F30][D182].
Total assets reached $4.42 trillion in FY2025, up 10.5%, with loans of $1.47 trillion and deposits of $2.56 trillion [F90][D218][X197][X207].
Loans were 57.3% of deposits, up from 55.0% in FY2024 but well below the 64.7% of FY2016 [D211][D188][D10].
The loan increase was driven by higher CIB Markets loans and securities-based lending in AWM on higher client demand [P4].
Shareholders' equity rose 5.1% to $362 billion, and the allowance for credit losses reached $25.8 billion, or 1.8% of loans [F110][D220][X216][D212].
Buybacks of $31.6 billion and dividends of $16.6 billion in FY2025 were funded alongside a $269.5 billion financing inflow [X102][X112][F80].
Net income for FY2021-FY2025 in the table comes from the proxy's pay-versus-performance table, not the 10-K, differing by up to 0.10%; the 10-K figure for FY2025 is $57.0 billion [R1][X20][F30].
Credit costs are rising: the provision climbed to $14.2 billion in FY2025 from $9.3 billion in FY2023, and criticized wholesale exposure rose to $48.5 billion from $44.7 billion [X147][X145][P2].
The criticized increase was driven by SPEs, Consumer & Retail, Banks & Finance Companies, Healthcare and Chemicals & Plastics, primarily from downgrades and new commitments [P2].
FY2020 pretax income and tax were later restated ($35.8 billion and $6.7 billion against $35.4 billion and $6.3 billion first reported); the pack uses the first-reported values [R2][R3][X63][X73].
Watch the efficiency ratio: a move above the 57.2% window median would reverse the FY2024-FY2025 improvement, reported in the FY2026 10-K [D333][D207].
Watch the provision as a share of revenue: holding above the 7.8% FY2025 level would extend the rise from 5.9% in FY2023 [D208][D161].
Watch net interest income growth: a return below the 3.1% FY2025 rate would signal the deposit margin compression cited in the FY2025 filing is persisting [D221][P28].
